newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle seen steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle seen steady to higher.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were expected to open steady to 0.150 cent per lb higher while feeder cattle were called steady to 0.100 cent higher, livestock analysts said.

Analysts anticipated carryover technical and fundamental strength in live cattle after posting new contract highs in the first four positions in Friday's trade. Higher boxed beef values Friday and expectations packers will have to raise bids for cash cattle should encourage demand, analysts said.
However, futures look overbought, especially with the large premium of futures to cash, they said.
Feeder cattle futures were seen following the lead of live cattle with early indications of further weakness in corn futures also expected to lend support, they said.
However, a lower CME feeder cattle index may limit upside potential, they added.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was down $0.05 at $82.12 per cwt.
